notes.title: We’re partnering with the European Space Agency for Mars Horizon 2: The Search for Life!
notes.content:
https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/31098357/17cb6ec82c57b0a837c95b3fd5816eb5bfd5c472.png

Hey everyone, we hope you’re having a great August so far! 

For those of you who are interested in all things space, you might have seen our upcoming game Mars Horizon 2: The Search for Life where you’ll be leading your space agency to investigate the solar system and collect evidence of life. Earlier this year we announced our partnership with Professor Konstantin Batygin, and now we have another exciting partnership to share with you! 

If you're one of those space lovers, you might have seen that the European Space Agency (ESA) are at Gamescom this year, which seems like a fitting time to let you all know that we are partnering with them once more for Mars Horizon 2: The Search for Life! 

The European Space Agency is Europe’s gateway to space. Its mission is to shape the development of Europe’s space capability and ensure that investment in space continues to deliver benefits to the citizens of Europe and the world.  

We are going to be working with the folks at ESA to make sure we can bring authenticity and real-world science into our sequel to Mars Horizon. As the sequel focuses on The Search for Life, we are excited to talk to them about biosignature detection, sample return, and much more. Their partnership ensures that we can create an authentic game in Mars Horizon 2, as we did with the first! 

Sign up to our Newsletter to be the first to hear about Alphas, Betas, and other news.

We're so excited to let you all know that Brewmaster: Beer Brewing Simulator is a finalist in the 2023 James Paul GEE Award in the Informal Learning category. People learn in all different ways and for many people games can be a brilliant tool for learning and understanding. This was a key focus for us when making the game, we worked hard to make it authentic and accessible.

Under the hood of Brewmaster is a real simulation of chemistry; so accurate and lifelike that it is possible to take recipes from a book on the subject and replicate them in the game to return the correct result. 
We wanted to help more people understand and appreciate the amazing world of brewing beer, and maybe inspire them to have a go at brewing themselves, if its something they've not done before. We are also very proud of our Brewpedia which has loads more info on all areas of the craft.
 
The GEE awards also includes the People's Choice awards and we'd love it if you could vote for us!

notes.title: Patch Notes: v1.0.6.5 (27th Oct 2022)
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40208531/61847dba1de9ddb25a9623cf3201bc79e128134b.png
Greetings Brewers! 🍻 
Our latest patch features a crate-full of bug fixes and improvements, as well as some eye-catching game posters to brighten up your workshops as part of our Indie Celebration Content Update. Enjoy!   

Improvements 
 Indie Celebration Content Update: added a selection of game posters that can be bought from the Catalogue (more will become available at each Mastery level in Brewmaster mode)  
 Added various new brewing hints 
 Resetting to default settings in options screens will now show a confirmation message before applying the change 
 Improved fade out of liquid puddles 
 Improved late game performance 
 Improved performance when looking at shelves with an item in hand 
 Improved translations in various languages 
Bug Fixes
 Fixed an issue where pumps would transfer solid ingredients, such as grains. You can now safely use pumps when transferring wort from your mash tuns 
 Recipes for Irish Red Ale, California Common, and Kellerbier will no longer ask players to ferment and condition at below room temperature 
 The Tooltip Delay setting in options will now correctly affect tooltips 
 Fixed an issue where Brewing Hints were set to “Advanced” by default, instead of “All Tips” 
 Fixed issue where containers could float in a spooky way when loading a save in which containers were placed on heat mats 
 Fixed an issue where the bottom part of electric kettles would vanish on loading a previous save 
 Electric kettles will now highlight properly when looked at 
 Fixed an issue where the tutorial would no longer display if loading from a Free Play game into a previous Brewmaster game where the tutorial was active 
 Fixed issue where incorrect input glyphs could show when switching to a mouse and keyboard 
 Fixed issue where the shortcut input for various confirm buttons wasn’t working 
 Fixed various issues with Brew Kettles, including not being able to place an immersion coil in the small Brew Kettle and their lids on/off state not saving properly 
 Fixed an issue where cosmetic items couldn’t be placed on a wall near the front door 
 Fixed an issue where picking up a container with multiple tubes attached when your inventory is already full could result in blocking equipping other items 
 The industrial coffee table (glass) and industrial crate should now be moveable in build mode 
 Fixed an issue where Imperial measurements would show oz instead of lb in recipes 
 Fixed various issues when using Imperial measurements in the Recipe Creator 
 Fixed issue where HUD warning messages could be cut off in various languages 
 Fixed some visual issues with overflowing liquid in various containers 
 Fixed various instances of unlocalised or incorrect text 
 Fixed various instances of overflowing text in different languages 
 Fixed incorrect translation for “To Boldy Gose” job requirement in Traditional Chinese 
 Fixed an issue where the “countdown” confirmation sometimes wouldn't count down correctly when changing display settings 
 Fixed an issue where the style matching tooltip in the tasting sequence was incorrectly rounding up some values (e.g. showing 5.9% ABV as 6.0%) 
 Fixed an issue where articles would be missing or not display entirely in the Brewpedia at certain UI scales 
 Fixed issue where it was possible to brew a beer with over 100% ABV, which is arguably a bit too strong 
As always, the team would like to give a huge hearty THANK YOU to all those who have left reviews here on Steam and helped spread the word about Brewmaster. Your support means the world to us.  And as always if you have any questions do let us know here on Steam, or over on our Discord. Have a brewtiful day!

notes.title: What IS Brewmaster: Beer Brewing Simulator? 🤔
notes.content:
Before we launch Brewmaster: Beer Brewing Simulator on September 29th for Steam and later in 2022 on PlayStation, Xbox, and Nintendo Switch, Matt (Lead Designer) and Peter (Lead Producer) wanted to give you a brief overview of what to expect in the game. We hope you find it useful before you steep your first grains!  🌾

___________________________________________________________________

Hello everyone, 

We’re both very excited for you to get your hands on Brewmaster. 

Development on the game started in June 2019 and from then we’ve had a clear idea of what we want to make. We thought we’d lay out what we’re aiming for with Brewmaster, so you can make up your own mind before purchasing if it sounds like something you’d be keen on playing. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40208531/a8f338e5fde98979338c4356cc9705b67d5505d2.png

What IS Brewmaster? ✔️
At its very core, Brewmaster is freeform brewing chemistry: it allows you to create beer using an authentic simulation of real brewing, with all the experimentation (and, occasionally, “happy little accidents”) that come up in homebrewing. 

It’s faithful to the craft of beer, and to the skills required in the hobby: creativity, patience, and an inquisitive mind. 

But we’re also lowering the barrier to entry for a hobby that can be seen by non-brewers as quite daunting to get into. If you’ve never consumed a beer in your life, or have no knowledge of brewing, Brewmaster will get you making beers and on the road to improving your skills with an in-depth tutorial where, by the end, you’ll have learned the fundamentals of real-world brewing. After that a lengthy Brewmaster Mode lets you master every aspect of beer whilst engaging with a story, completing jobs, and entering competitions. 

It’s also a very chill game. The vibe we’ve gone for is cosy and positive, and with the characters from the in-game community of homebrewers, we’ve really tried to reflect the diverse and independent spirit of homebrewing. Have a listen to Iron & Wine’s Naked As We Came - we hope it feels like how that song feels. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40208531/6102b09865f9a9a7f610a0ee9d2ff105004a9d5d.png

What ISN’T Brewmaster?  ❌
First, this isn’t a cheaply-made throwaway experience. A lot of love has gone into Brewmaster, with lots of attention paid to the visuals, the simulation, the amount of content, and so on. 

Second, it’s not tedious and po-faced (it’s not a chemistry exam or, forbid the thought, an edutainment game!), but it’s also not slapstick or a game with “kerrr-azy" physics. It’s a more deliberately paced, relaxed experience. 

And on that subject, it’s also not a business management game. You’re not running a massive brewery and pumping out millions of hectolitres in a harsh and competitive landscape where your livelihood is under threat; you’re enjoying a hobby which, later in the game, might get you some attention from independent craft breweries and a hearty pat on the back from the local community. 

 From both of us, and the whole team at Auroch, we hope this sounds like something that’s right for you. If it is, please support us by purchasing the game and, if you’ve the inclination, leave us a review letting us know your thoughts! 

___________________________________________________________________

Brewmaster: Beer Brewing Simulator will launch on September 29th on Steam, with the PlayStation, Xbox, and Nintendo Switch versions launching at a later date in 2022. Add the game to your wishlist on Steam here. We can’t wait for you all to experience it! 😊

notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40208531/984e2668d2e13e102a2a503055db45d57aaba3c4.png

A massive thank you for all of the feedback, it really helps us understand how you play. We will be continually updating this post as we hear more from you. So keep checking back if you need help! 🍻

Getting started in Brewmaster: Beer Brewing Simulator


 Start off by opening the “Brewer’s Quarterly” magazine near the front door
 Choose one of the jobs in the Brewer’s Quarterly, and then a recipe that will meet the requirements of the job
 Recipes can be pinned to the HUD via the recipes section in the Brewer’s Quarterly or in your journal
 Use your watch (T on keyboard / LT on controller) to accelerate time
 To skip larger amounts of time, use the calendar in the workshop
 To see the temperature of a liquid, activate X-ray mode when looking at the container
 To transfer liquids to Conditioning Containers, you’ll have to use a tube
 When using tubes, make sure the target container is lower than the first, so gravity can do its work
 If your final brew isn’t large enough to qualify as a small batch, try adding more water to get it closer to 20L
 If things go wrong with your brew, don’t worry - just return to the start of the recipe. Brewing is a learning experience!

Contamination in Brewmaster
There are various times in the brewing process where contamination can creep into your brew, such as leaving off the lid during the fermentation stage, or leaving it ON during the boil. This can be seen by the amount of "off" flavours in your beer. The lower the Contamination, the higher the quality of the beer. Contamination can be reduced by good brewing practices, such as leaving the lid off when boiling wort so that unwanted chemicals can escape.


 We've also got an FAQ you can check out with more information about the game.

About Moor Beer
Started in 2007, Moor Beer Company are one of Britain’s most respected craft brewers, with sites in Bristol and London. They were the originators of Natural Live Beer, the vegan beer movement, and can-conditioned real ale, all of which forever changed the world of brewing and paved the way for many others to follow. They have been awarded countless times, including Brewer of the Year by the British Guild of Beer Writers and were one of only 16 breweries, and the smallest and youngest, to be given a Golden Award by the Campaign for Real Ale (CAMRA) in their 50th anniversary honours. More about Moor at www.moorbeer.co.uk.

“Working with Auroch has been great and we’re thrilled they chose us. I grew Moor Beer out of my homebrewing background, so it was really nostalgic and fun to see this replicated virtually – even down to my original orange picnic cooler mash tun! This will be a great game for people to dip their toe into the world of brewing, and if you get immersed in it as much as I did then you might also wind up with your own brewery.” — Justin Hawke, Head Brewer and owner of Moor Beer

Because the Public Alpha has again been our focus this month, the code team has mostly been making this area of the game as stable as possible before now and then. 

 The art team has been hard at work on tidying up some of the liquid visuals and creating more furniture, some of which you’ll see in the Public Alpha. We’ve been continuing to “skin” big chunks of the user interface to give you a better idea of how the final thing will all look, plus working on the portraits for some of the characters you’ll meet in the game. We can’t wait for you to see how Jeff and the gang have turned out. 
 Audio has completed its first pass of everything in the game and it’s sounding really good so far. Still some tweaks to go, but Brewmaster is now very pleasant to listen to on a decent set of headphones – let us know what you think of the birdsong 😉 
 Our designers have been working hard too, with the majority of the meta systems now designed and waiting to be implemented. You won’t see these in the Public Alpha but, hey, if this test all goes well and you’d like us to run another one like it in the future, let us know, and we can think about getting a Public Beta organised for next year...

Right now the development team is heavily focused on the Public Alpha with a particular emphasis on fixing bugs and getting the “feel” of the game good. Part of that “feel” comes from audio, which is coming along at a grand old pace. It’s also wonderfully cosy to just be in the brewing room listening to the ambience of the birds tweeting, while you think about what beer you’re going to make next. 

💻 Coding 💻
The code team’s been smashing bugs that our intrepid QA team has been finding, but it’s also started throwing the game at more consoles and upgrading to the latest and greatest version of Unreal Engine 4, to see what works and what doesn’t after doing this - luckily, not a lot has gone wrong so far!

 📝 Design 📝
What’s the design team been up to? Well, they’re working on the meta systems of the game: such as how you progress, what kind of tasks you’ll take on, and how this will all be presented. Our UI/UX team has been creating a kit to make the UI skinning process as smooth as possible, and so far it’s looking 😘👌

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40208531/149c4825d5b0e2cc5cc451125f8905e8a8e747d2.gif
🍻 Working on core gameplay 🍻
Is it the end of August already? Time flies when you’re developing a video game about brewing beer, as the old saying goes.

We’ve been working on core gameplay the mostly this month, ensuring our first sets of objects are in and that you can use them to brew a beer; from getting out the equipment and ingredients from a cupboard, all the way to inspecting a finished brew. Mash tuns, stainless steel pans, fermentation containers, tubes, immersion coils, gas burners, ingredient packets, water taps… there’s a lot, and while there’s plenty of bugs right now, it’s all pretty much there.

Excitingly, our producer at Sold Out - Brewmaster’s publisher - put Brewmaster’s chemical simulation to the test the other day and tried to make an IPA from a real life recipe book he had on his homebrewing bookshelf. And lo and behold, out popped an IPA! We’ll drink to that! 😊👍

But hey, why read about what’s been going on, when you can see what we’ve done instead 👇

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40208531/c1a7d65c061b85cf3b4213eced1f12840a77cb75.png
[L-R; Programmer, Andres, Programmer, Jack, and Finance & Admin Assistant Danielle]
🎉 Auroch visits a Beer Festival 🎉
Brandon, Danielle, Andres, and Jack went to Bristol Craft Beer Festival on July 30th (yes that was technically last month but it was right at the end!) and tried a whole selection of beers; getting a lot of inspiration from talking to the brewers and other beer fans. 

Associate Designer, Brandon, said his favourite was Alternating Currants" by Brixton Brewery, a mixed berry sour. 🥫🍓 They have awesome can designs too! Our Finance and Admin Assistant, Danielle, is normally more of a cider drinker but she really enjoyed Jubel Beers as they were so fruity and tasty. She said if she had to pick a favourite it’d be the elderflower one. 🍎🍑🍐

One of our Brewmaster programmers, Andres, really enjoyed the New Bristol Salted Chocolate Bigger Cinder Toffee Stout. 🍫 He said it’s really easy to drink and full of amazing flavors. Jack is also a programmer and his favourite was an Arbor and Wiper And True collaboration, a sour beer blend. Both brewery's barrel aged a beer then blended them together. It was much smoother than many sours, but still with an edge to it and a lovely depth of flavour.

Don't be fooled though! We are still a way off completing development. But doesn't it look great?

Take a look at our new pouring! Liquids in general are really difficult to get looking right digitally, so pouring liquids dynamically is even more difficult. We've spent so much time working on this, and we're getting super close to to being happy with it.

When you pour too much water (or beer) into your glass it can overflow. It happens to the best of us, and will not doubt happen to all of us when we first get our hands on Brewmaster. So of course we want to include some nice overflowing in the game. 

We've also been working on how our beers will look, by working on the shader that powers them all. Just have a look at that in action in this tweet, doesn't it make you thirsty? The water and the wort is looking pretty great too. It gets us bubbling with excitement! Haha, get it?

We've been busy working on making more brewing equipment and different ingredient assets too. Right now our artists are working closely with our code team to get one kind of every object you need into the game to be able to brew a beer from start to finish. We'll hopefully be able to show you all of this in the very near future.

Not only all of that *gestures at above* but our chemical simulation has made great strides too, with absolutely loads of data for ingredients now our system. 🧪Chemical Simulation🧪
One of the biggest challenges in making our game is in the simulation of brewing chemistry. Brewmaster isn’t simply a case of hop + malt + yeast + water = beer. Rather it’s a complex system that tracks things like…

 How much of the specific flavours from hops go into a brew, based on when they’re added
 How much of the fermentable sugars are converted by the yeast into alcohol before it’s killed off
 How much of the water is lost to evaporation
… and so on.

We're spending a lot of time on this area of the game, as it’s at the very heart of the gameplay and will offer a huge variety of outcomes for players to experiment with.

There’s still a lot more work to be done, but currently you can use the systems we’ve built to brew something resembling a beer. As we’re yet to balance all the data the simulation is pulling from, we wouldn’t want to drink the beer we’ve managed to make, but give it time. Right now our team is able to look under-the-hood and see what the chemsim is doing using placeholder menus and graphs, which is a huge step forward in getting it feeling right.

⏰Time passing in Brewmaster⏰
People have been asking us about how time works in the game; wondering whether they’ll need to wait two weeks of real time in order to reach the end of a fermentation, or even longer for a barrel-aged stout. As you’ll have seen from our day/night cycle video, the game works in realtime but also allows you to speed up the passing of time, so you don't have to wait.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40208531/88bbc818b499a4ba4066f3f75d3353222b32512b.png

🥛Liquid Pouring🥛
Next, let’s talk about liquid pouring. We’re really proud of the announcement trailer we made for the game, however, this was using early concept visualisations and those liquids pouring visuals aren’t what we’re having in the full release. We've been working hard on the liquid pouring and it's now looking really great. We will be able to show you these soon so make sure to stick around for more developer updates. We will also be bringing you at look at overflowing liquid in future updates too! We can't wait for you to make a mess of your kitchens.

🎮UX/UI development🎮
UX/UI is one of those things that most people don’t notice (until it isn’t working well), but it’s an incredibly important discipline at our studio. Because of this, we’re building the game to work comfortably with both keyboard and mouse, and controllers, so the UX/UI team is hard at work creating wireframes for the game to get the positioning of each onscreen element just right.

There’s loads more going on, and plenty more to show, but we’ll save that for another update in the near future!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40208531/8372e5bfee2447e2d584605366a2b05d78e70142.pngWhat are your thoughts on beer and gaming!
We are running a survey about Brewmaster to help us plan the next steps we take. We need to hear from YOU, our Brewmaster community.

As a thank you, people who fill in this survey will be entered into a giveaway and one lucky winner will get £25 worth of Steam credit. The survey will take about 5 minutes to complete. Thanks for helping us!

 Fill in the Brewmaster survey here

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40208531/15b0ec92407a0d9a9ca1c54614155c7ca46c3ee2.png
Brewmaster in The MIX 
We hope everyone had an exciting E3 week. Brewmaster was part of the Play For All Showcase, a showcase from the partnership of GameSpot and The MIX. With a focus on Indie games, especially those from diverse backgrounds, so we were delighted to be invited along. 

It was so cool to be involved in The MIX alongside so many other awesome games and studios.

Catch up with our Steam post about The MIX here!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40208531/3ab43c4bf0f825bdcc59bcd2101f3db5635e16cb.png
 Matt brews Auroch Digit-ale 🍾
Our Lead Game Designer for Brewmaster has been brewing his own beer at home. As we’re making a first-person homebrewing simulator we feel it's important that the team have plenty of hands-on experience. He made an IPA and named it Auroch Digit-ale! 

Here's what Matt had to say after his beer brewing experience:

"Brewing my own beer was definitely useful when it comes to designing the game. Homebrewing as a hobby can appear intimidatingly complex from the outside - so it’s very important we get players over that barrier, and get them brewing beer as quickly as possible."

"It’s key that we show players that, at its core, the brewing process is quite straightforward. Then when they know the basics, we can show them just how much lies beyond - how much room for creative expression, experimentation, and mastery there is. As a hobby, it’s endlessly rewarding - it’s our job to convey that in the game."

"I crammed all the gear into my kitchen, scared the dog with the world’s largest stainless steel pan, and bought some obscenely bitter hops. At the end of it all, I had around 30 bottles of beer that was darker and a little maltier than I expected, and that could be anywhere between 3% and 6% ABV - but it was still recognisable as an IPA and, most importantly, was actually drinkable!"

notes.title: A small update, and a big thank you, from the Brewmaster Team
notes.content:
Hi everyone, we’re the team behind Brewmaster 🍻

We’ve been blown away by the support you’ve shown for our game - so a huge thank you from us! We’re an indie studio with a small dedicated team who are passionate about games and homebrewing, so we really appreciate it. Your excitement for Brewmaster is inspiring and motivates us to make the best game we possibly can.

Right now we’re working hard behind the scenes, developing our chemistry simulation, building our virtual brewing space, and all the equipment in the game, and making the beer look oh so good. We can’t wait to share it with you.

We’ll be posting updates about development on Steam throughout the process to keep you in the loop. We’ll also be posting behind-the-scenes GIFs and images on Steam and socials so you can see how good it’s looking. Make sure you follow us on Twitter to see them.

If you want to know more about our thought process behind creating the game check out our article on the PlayStation Blog. 

Lastly, make sure you’re signed up to our Brewmaster Mailing List - we’ll be using this list to find players for our alpha and beta testing for the game, as well as sending around updates during development. It's really important to us to hear your feedback during these testing phases so we can make Brewmaster even more awesome, we love hearing from our community and getting your input.


 Sign up to the Brewmaster mailing list


Once again, thank you for supporting us, we have lots of exciting things to show you soon.

The Brewmaster Team 🍻
